arxiv-2108-11511.title: Bayesian Estimation of the Hydroxyl Radical Diffusion Coefficient at Low Temperature and High Pressure from Atomistic Molecular Dynamics
arxiv-2108-11511.creator: Carter T. Butts, Rachel W. Martin
arxiv-2108-11511.description: Abstract The hydroxyl radical is the primary reactive oxygen species produced by the radiolysis of water, and is a significant source of radiation damage to living organisms. Mobility of the hydroxyl radical at low temperatures and/or high pressures is hence a potentially important factor in determining the challenges facing psychrophilic and/or barophilic organisms in high-radiation environments (e.g.

arxiv-2207-13243.title: Toward Transparent AI: A Survey on Interpreting the Inner Structures of Deep Neural Networks
arxiv-2207-13243.creator: Tilman Räuker ∗, Anson Ho ∗, Stephen Casper ∗, Dylan Hadfield-Menell
arxiv-2207-13243.description: Abstract The last decade of machine learning has seen drastic increases in scale and capabilities. Deep neural networks (DNNs) are increasingly being deployed in the real world. However, they are difficult to analyze, raising concerns about using them without a rigorous understanding of how they function.

arxiv-2212-04814.title: The Falsification Adaptive Set in Linear Models with Instrumental Variables that Violate the Exclusion or Conditional Exogeneity Restriction
arxiv-2212-04814.creator: Nicolas Apfel, Frank Windmeijer
arxiv-2212-04814.description: Abstract Masten and Poirier 2021 introduced the falsification adaptive set ( FAS ) in linear models with a single endogenous variable estimated with multiple correlated instrumental variables (IVs). The FAS reflects the model uncertainty that arises from falsification of the baseline model.

arxiv-2306-06393.title: On the required radio resources for ultra-reliable communication in highly interfered scenarios
arxiv-2306-06393.creator: Gilberto Berardinelli, Ramoni Adeogun
arxiv-2306-06393.description: Abstract Future wireless systems are expected to support mission-critical services demanding higher and higher reliability. In this letter, we dimension the radio resources needed to achieve a given failure probability target for ultra-reliable wireless systems in high interference conditions, assuming a protocol with frequency hopping combined with packet repetitions.

arxiv-2308-02801.title: DiCuPIT: Distributed Cuckoo Filter-based Pending Interest Table
arxiv-2308-02801.creator: Arman Mahmoudi, Mahmood Ahmadi
arxiv-2308-02801.description: Abstract Named data networking is one of the recommended architectures for the future of the Internet. In this communication architecture, the content name is used instead of the IP address. To achieve this purpose, a new data structure is added to the nodes of named data networking which is called Pending Interest Table (PIT).

arxiv-2404-16252.title: Stabilization of hyperbolic reaction-diffusion systems on directed networks through the generalized Routh-Hurwitz criterion for complex polynomials
arxiv-2404-16252.creator: Riccardo Muolo 1†, Anthony Hastir 2,3 and Hiroya Nakao 1
arxiv-2404-16252.description: Abstract The study of dynamical systems on complex networks is of paramount importance in engineering, given that many natural and artificial systems find a natural embedding on discrete topologies. For instance, power grids, chemical reactors and the brain, to name a few, can be modeled through the network formalism by considering elementary units coupled via the links.

arxiv-2407-09606.title: Towards 𝔸 1 \mathbb{A}^{1} -homotopy theory of rigid analytic spaces
arxiv-2407-09606.creator: Christian Dahlhausen, Can Yaylali
arxiv-2407-09606.description: Abstract † † 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: 14F42, 14G22 To any rigid analytic space (in the sense of Fujiwara–Kato) we assign an 𝔸 1 \mathbb{A}^{1} -invariant rigid analytic homotopy category with coefficients in any presentable category. We show some functorial properties of this assignment as a functor on the category of rigid analytic spaces.

pmc-10575960.title: Functional characterization of a lytic polysaccharide monooxygenase from Schizophyllum commune that degrades non-crystalline substrates
pmc-10575960.creator: Heidi Østby, Idd A Christensen, Karen Hennum, Anikó Várnai, Edith Buchinger, Siri Grandal, Gaston Courtade, Olav A Hegnar, Finn L Aachmann, Vincent G H Eijsink
pmc-10575960.description: Lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (LPMOs) are mono-copper enzymes that use O2 or H2O2 to oxidatively cleave glycosidic bonds. LPMOs are prevalent in nature, and the functional variation among these enzymes is a topic of great interest. We present the functional characterization of one of the 22 putative AA9-type LPMOs from the fungus Schizophyllum commune, ScLPMO9A.

pmc-11428807.title: Securing human resources for Japan’s aging population: a mixed methods study of job satisfaction and well-being among Southeast Asian long-term care workers in Japan
pmc-11428807.creator: Niaya Harper Igarashi, Junko Kiriya, Rogie Royce Carandang, Ken Ing Cherng Ong, Akira Shibanuma, Masamine Jimba
pmc-11428807.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundJapan is one of the countries experiencing a “super-aged society.” The government has looked to Southeast Asia for recruiting workers to fill the demand for long-term care (LTC) workers. However, migrant LTC workers have faced many job-related stressors. This study aimed to examine the factors associated with job satisfaction and subjective well-being among Filipino, Indonesian, and Vietnamese LTC workers in Japan and explore the specific factors behind what makes them satisfied in their jobs.MethodsA convergent mixed methods study was conducted.

pmc-11521331.title: A consensus-based classification workflow to determine genetically inferred ancestry from comprehensive genomic profiling of patients with solid tumors
pmc-11521331.creator: Zachary D Wallen, Mary K Nesline, Sarabjot Pabla, Shuang Gao, Erik Vanroey, Stephanie B Hastings, Heidi Ko, Kyle C Strickland, Rebecca A Previs, Shengle Zhang, Jeffrey M Conroy, Taylor J Jensen, Elizabeth George, Marcia Eisenberg, Brian Caveney, Pratheesh Sathyan, Shakti Ramkissoon, Eric A Severson
pmc-11521331.description: Disparities in cancer diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes based on self-identified race and ethnicity (SIRE) are well documented, yet these variables have historically been excluded from clinical research. Without SIRE, genetic ancestry can be inferred using single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) detected from tumor DNA using comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP).

pmc-11935600.title: Viral Infection and Ischemic Stroke: Emerging Trends and Mechanistic Insights
pmc-11935600.creator: Michael Clarke, Sarina Falcione, Roobina Boghozian, Raluca Todoran, Yiran Zhang, Maria Guadalupe C. Real, Alexis StPierre, Twinkle Joy, Glen C. Jickling
pmc-11935600.description: Population studies have suggested that viral infections may be contributing to risk of ischemic stroke, although the mechanisms for this are unclear. In this review, we examine the epidemiological evidence supporting the involvement of viral diseases, including influenza, COVID‐19, chronic herpesvirus infections, and hepatitis C in current trends of stroke incidence.

pmc-12470434.title: Comparison of Fracture Resistance Using Two Different Major Cemented Stems in Osteoporotic Bone Models
pmc-12470434.creator: Kohei Hashimoto, Yukio Nakamura, Nobunori Takahashi, Takkan Morishima
pmc-12470434.description: Background: Periprosthetic hip fractures (PPFs) are one of the major complications in total hip arthroplasty (THA). Therefore, it is important to identify a mechanism for fracture resistance in THA. This study aimed to clarify the differences in fracture torque and fracture type analysis between two different types of cemented stems.

pmc-13135772.title: Mild Oculocutaneous Albinism Type 1B With Subtle Cutaneous Findings: A Dermatology-Oriented Case Report
pmc-13135772.creator: Catalina Montané, Diego Guarda, Priscilla Marquez, Gerardo Bascuñan
pmc-13135772.description: Oculocutaneous albinism type 1B (OCA1B) may present with subtle dermatologic manifestations and be initially suspected through ophthalmologic abnormalities. We report a 16-year-old female with normal psychomotor development who presented with progressive decreased visual acuity beginning in childhood. Ophthalmologic evaluation demonstrated reduced best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and fundoscopic findings, including pale optic discs and increased visibility of choroidal vessels.

pmc-13250237.title: Efficacy and Safety of Normal Saline Injection for Corticosteroid‐Induced Cutaneous Atrophy: A Systematic Review
pmc-13250237.creator: Jia Qi Adam Bai, Jennifer V. H. Tran, Chaocheng Liu
pmc-13250237.description: le, accessible, and minimally invasive treatment option, although their efficacy and safety remain insufficiently established. This systematic review summarizes the evidence on the efficacy and safety of NS injections in the management of corticosteroid‐induced cutaneous atrophy. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered on PROSPERO (CRD420251274107).

pmc-13374067.title: The development and utility of frameworks designed to evaluate research capacity building initiatives in healthcare settings: a methodological review
pmc-13374067.creator: Olivia A. King, Ella Ottrey, Michele Conlin, Sze Lin Yoong, Anna Wong Shee, Emma West, Laura Alston, Joanne Porter, Catherine E. Huggins
pmc-13374067.description: BackgroundBuilding research capacity in health settings is essential for improving the relevance and application of health research. Rigorous evaluation of research capacity in health settings optimizes the development, implementation and improvement of such initiatives. Cooke’s 2005 framework was the earliest peer-reviewed framework to evaluate research capacity in health settings.

pmc-13430747.title: Diagnostic and therapeutic gaps in recurrent stroke management: real-world insights from a Ghanaian hospital-based registry
pmc-13430747.creator: Priscilla Abrafi Opare-Addo, Fred Stephen Sarfo, Minas Aikins, Enock Asante, Maxwell Nyanaah, Nana Osei Asibey Derkyi, Jessey Mahama Holu, Gordon Manu Amponsah
pmc-13430747.description: BackgroundRecurrent strokes account for up to 1 out of 4 strokes in Low-and-Middle-Income-Countries (LMICs), culminating in worsening of outcomes. International guidelines recommend subtype-specific etiological workup to help tailor strategies for prevention of recurrence after an index stroke. However, huge gaps in secondary stroke prevention persist in LMICs.

pmc-13683044.title: Effects of a randomized controlled trial of unconditional cash transfers on epigenetic measures of ageing and cognition in children and mothers
pmc-13683044.creator: Laurel Raffington, Yayouk E. Willems, Jessica F. Sperber, Sepideh Zarandooz, Molly A. Costanzo, Daniel A. Notterman, Colter Mitchell, Elliot M. Tucker-Drob, Greg J. Duncan, Nathan A. Fox, Lisa A. Gennetian, Katherine A. Magnuson, Sonya V. Troller-Renfree, Hirokazu Yoshikawa, Elisabeth B. Binder, K.
pmc-13683044.description: Here we present epigenetic findings from a randomized controlled trial studying the impact of unconditional cash gifts of US$333 per month (children n = 313; mothers n = 329) or US$20 per month (children n = 423; mothers n = 448) to US mothers with low income during their child’s first four years of life.
